key_insight: SAGE-PINN embeds axisymmetric cylindrical geometry directly into a PINN, eliminating the r=0 singularity while enforcing mass conservation and boundary conditions by construction.
engineering_relevance: It enables label-free surrogate simulation of coupled flow and heat transfer in axisymmetric biomedical and multiphysics problems, such as stenosed artery transport, with stable performance across a broad operating range.
method: Uses parity-preserving variable s=r^2 and a modified stream-function formulation to remove explicit 1/r singular terms.
Enforces boundary conditions exactly with boundary-fitted analytical ansätze.
Stabilizes training with staged momentum-thermal-joint optimization, residual normalization, Péclet/Richardson continuation, and a physics-scaled drift guard.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions for steady nanofluid flow and heat transfer, achieving single-precision mass conservation and up to 1.6% axial-velocity and 9.1% temperature relative L2 error in the central operating range.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-influenced slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer, so regime coverage and continuation settings matter.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
